operations.original: [F1] A set is atlas-null when every chart image in that atlas is Euclidean null ([[def-null-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold]]).
operations.proposed: [F1] In positive dimension, a set is atlas-null when every chart image in that atlas is Euclidean null; in dimension zero atlas-nullity means the set is empty ([[def-null-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold]]).

operations.original: [L1] Local coordinate diffeomorphisms preserve Euclidean nullity on suitably small source and target chart neighbourhoods ([[lem-c1-local-diffeomorphisms-preserve-null-sets-locally]]).
operations.proposed:
[L1] For a $C^1$ map and prescribed source and target charts, each point of a compact source set has a neighbourhood on whose closure the coordinate representative is Lipschitz ([[lem-a-c1-map-is-locally-lipschitz-on-compact-coordinate-subsets]]).

[F2] Charts belonging to the same smooth structure have smooth transition maps in their displayed coordinates; in particular the identity map has $C^1$ coordinate representatives ([[def-smooth-manifold]], [[def-smoothly-compatible-charts]]).

[F3] An open subset of a smooth manifold carries its restricted smooth structure ([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

[L4] Global Lipschitz maps $\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m$ preserve Euclidean null sets, and Euclidean nullity passes to subsets ([[thm-lipschitz-images-of-null-sets-in-rn-are-null]], [[def-null-and-content-zero-in-rn]]).

operations.original: 1.1 Assume $E$ is $\mathcal A$-null and fix $(V,\psi)\in\mathcal B$. The overlaps $V\cap U$ with $(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal A$ cover $V$. At each point of each overlap, [L1] gives a smaller open neighbourhood $W$ on which the coordinate transition $\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}$ preserves Euclidean nullity in both directions. These $W$ form an open cover of $V$. Apply [L2] under the given countable choice to obtain a countable cover $(W_j)$ subordinate to these local transition neighbourhoods, and use [A1] to fix a containing local transition neighbourhood and its source chart $(U_j,\varphi_j)$ for each $j$. [A1, L1, L2, given]
operations.proposed: 1.1 If $\dim M=0$, [F1] says that either atlas declares $E$ null exactly when $E=\varnothing$, proving the equivalence. Assume now $m=\dim M\ge1$, that $E$ is $\mathcal A$-null, and fix $(V,\psi)\in\mathcal B$. For $(U,\varphi)\in\mathcal A$ and $p\in U\cap V$, set $T=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}$ on $\varphi(U\cap V)$. By [F2], $T$ is $C^1$. Apply [L1] to the identity of $M$, the restricted source chart $(U\cap V,\varphi)$, the target chart $(V,\psi)$, and the compact set $\{p\}$. It supplies an open neighbourhood $O$ of $p$ in $U\cap V$ on whose coordinate closure $T$ is Lipschitz. Choose a closed cube $Q\subseteq\varphi(O)$ with $\varphi(p)$ in its interior and put $W=\varphi^{-1}(\operatorname{int}Q)$. These $W$, with all their displayed chart and cube witnesses, form an open cover of $V$. [F1, F2, L1, given, cases, choose, construct]

operations.original: 2.1 Since $E$ is $\mathcal A$-null, each $\varphi_j(E\cap W_j)$ is null as a subset of $\varphi_j(E\cap U_j)$. The chartwise conclusion of [L1], on the local neighbourhood containing $W_j$, gives that $C_j=\psi(E\cap W_j)$ is Euclidean null. The countable family $(W_j)$ covers $V$, so $\psi(E\cap V)=\bigcup_j C_j$. [F1, L1, step 1.1]
operations.proposed:
1.2 Write $Q=\prod_{i<m}[a_i,b_i]$ and define $r_Q:\mathbb R^m\to Q$ by $(r_Q(x))_i=\min\{b_i,\max\{a_i,x_i\}\}$. Each scalar clamp changes distances by at most the original distance; summing the squares gives $\|r_Q(x)-r_Q(y)\|_2\le\|x-y\|_2$. Thus $T\circ r_Q$ is a global Lipschitz map and agrees with $T$ on $\varphi(W)$. Since $\varphi(E\cap W)$ is a subset of the null set $\varphi(E\cap U)$, [L4] gives that $\psi(E\cap W)=(T\circ r_Q)(\varphi(E\cap W))$ is null in the prescribed $\psi$ coordinates. [F1, L4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.1 View $V$ as an open smooth manifold by [F3]. Apply [L2] to its cover from step 1.1, obtaining a finite or countable subordinate coordinate-ball cover $(W_j)_{j\ge0}$, with the empty or finite case handled by empty sets after the last term. Use [A1] to select a containing member $W$ and its chart and cube witnesses for each nonempty $W_j$. By step 1.2 and the subset clause of [L4], $C_j=\psi(E\cap W_j)$ is Euclidean null. Since these sets cover $E\cap V$, $\psi(E\cap V)=\bigcup_{j\ge0}C_j$. [F3, L2, A1, L4, step 1.1, step 1.2, choose]

operations.original: Interchanging $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ gives the reverse implication. [A1, L3, step 2.1] ∎
operations.proposed: Interchanging $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ gives the reverse implication; step 1.1 already covers dimension zero. [A1, L3, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

operations.original: [A1] Countable choice selects one arbitrarily small cube-cover sequence for each member of a countable null family ([[def-countable-choice]]).
operations.proposed: [A1] Countable choice selects one witness from each set in a countable family of nonempty witness sets; in particular it selects cube-cover sequences for countable null families ([[def-countable-choice]]).
